title: Low-rank adaptation

paper.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
paper.year_note: Original/preprint year except GCN (2017 venue, 2016 preprint) and speculative decoding (2023 venue, 2022 preprint).

statement: Implement Low-rank adaptation: fine-tune low-rank residual adapters with at most one percent trainable parameters and frozen base weights. Read the linked paper and isolate the named mechanism. Write a self-contained solve(data), fit using training tensors only, and return Submission(model=model). Keep validation labels out of fitting and preprocessing. This is an educational reduced-scale adaptation, not a claim to reproduce original paper results. Use licensed-adaptation-corpus; required output: Base-model input -> task logits; <=1 percent trainable parameters. Evaluate task_quality (maximize). Freeze base weights; low-rank delta merge agrees with unmerged output. Required ablation: Compare ranks at fixed trainable-parameter budget. Curriculum draft: reference, task-specific objective/evaluation adaptation and thresholds remain unimplemented; a named dataset may have a loader but this does not make this model executable. The provided solution raises NotImplementedError.

dataset.description: Freeze base weights; low-rank delta merge agrees with unmerged output
dataset.split_policy: Disjoint train/validation/test examples; fit preprocessing using training data only.

budget.note: Provisional safety caps, not empirically calibrated GPU budgets.

checks: Return a Submission containing a torch module.
Do not read validation labels during fitting.
No NaN or infinite outputs; obey parameter cap.
Freeze base weights; low-rank delta merge agrees with unmerged output

ablation.change: Compare ranks at fixed trainable-parameter budget
ablation.control: Same split, seed, training steps and optimizer.
ablation.report: Report metric and parameter/time deltas honestly; do not infer superiority from one seed.
